title: Sharpen the many-axis prime product bound to exp(1/3) (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the sharp product-loss envelope implied by ToikY #4029's many-axis prime band, with the actual axis count D=d-1:

```diff
- T/S < 3/2
+ T/S < (3d/(3d-1))^(d-1) < exp(1/3) < 349/250
```

Claim type: **scoped mathematical proof with finite corroboration**. The finite-d envelope is the exact supremum under the band inequalities, and exp(1/3) is their least uniform upper bound. Sharpness permits rational band points; prime-restricted sharpness remains open. No prime-supply cutoff, physical caller admission, selected frontier or kappa changes.

Only `research/many-axis-prime-product-loss/` is added. The original card is explicitly changed to this algebraic side result. Scientific base is `a5df48c55ea806d7952b65acc9c76d878ff09b13`, priority revision 7. The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19144301) matches the delivered scope. Research stopped at this first verified improvement.

## Evidence

- Before: #4029 supplied the band and a sufficient 3/2 product bound. After: the new elementary product/logarithm proof gives the exact finite-d envelope, its uniform limit and an explicit admissible rational sequence approaching it. The logarithmic inequalities are standard; the new contribution is the caller-specific sharp envelope.
- Local warning-strict normal and optimized CPython 3.12.15 checks pass: 1,364 complete rational boxes, 511 finite-d logarithmic comparisons, 504 endpoint approaches, sixteen limit probes, nine invalid-input rejections and two boundary counterexamples. The two registered commands took 0.219 and 0.220 seconds, below their 120-second limits. These are check durations, not speedup claims.
- Registered metadata/pins and both scientific commands pass. Committed-byte/full-source-history preflight passes on `91a444590bdf7547903c16873064e6398e55f9d3`. Official export integrity and isolated normal/optimized Git-free replays pass with an empty executable PATH; all six exported files retain identical hashes. Syntax/function-size inspection passes, with twelve functions and a longest function of 27 lines.
- The verifier prints a generated receipt bound to all five package files. It imports no predecessor executable and does not replay predecessor scientific results. Historical provenance is pinned in SOURCES.json; there are no external runtime inputs or dependencies.

Exact reproduction commands from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/many-axis-prime-product-loss/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/many-axis-prime-product-loss/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/many-axis-prime-product-loss
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/many-axis-prime-product-loss --check-source-history
```

Substitute another local CPython 3.12 path as needed. Expected markers are `PASS_MANY_AXIS_PRIME_PRODUCT_LOSS`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations and credit

The proof assumes the displayed band and D=d-1. It covers every dimension algebraically, with finite checks as corroboration. Integer/prime sharpness, prime abundance, source production and source admission are not proved here. No giant prime search, encoded producer, numerical recovery, physical routing/restoration/stock/precision/tape invoice, selected scientific cold replay, Lean or Docker was run. No complete multiplication theorem is claimed. The historical card baseline raises `KeyError: 'bit_lower'` against the current selected schema and is unchanged. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

Credit ToikY #4029 for the band, axis-count reading, prime construction and prior bound; unpaidmoon #4142 for the encoded-guard boundary; Jose Manuel #3935; Tekalign #4024; Cinna Davis; Chafik Boukhalfa; Josie Elliston; the retained source08 authors; and Harvey and van der Hoeven. Fiori, Kadiri and Swidinsky's analytic input belongs to the predecessor's supply theorem and is not used by this algebraic consequence. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Frozen sources and predecessor attribution are unchanged.

## Related open work

Own-account open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-23T10:58:25Z were refreshed before DONE. One studies the same prime band:

- #5149 lowers the sufficient prime-supply cutoff and retains the predecessor's product bound. This result sharpens the product-loss envelope and does not derive a prime-supply cutoff. No competing number is computed and no extra cross-check of that contribution was run.

The other refreshed submissions concern Neumann tails, character sums, stable-lane reversal, Gaussian inverse edges, a projection recurrence, rounding guards and E8/P112 factorization floors. None studies this product-loss envelope; no additional comparison computations were run.

## Open next questions

1. Is exp(1/3) also sharp for distinct primes in the retained two-scale domain? Begin with a narrowing interval above the lower band endpoint; uniform prime abundance there remains unproved.
2. Can a fully charged selection policy near the upper endpoint guarantee a smaller loss? Begin with an actual caller's gap, period and prime-queue contracts; availability and producer cost remain blockers.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed on exact contribution head `91a444590bdf7547903c16873064e6398e55f9d3` in [run 39943684548](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39943684548): planning in 6m9s and the focused package replay in 1m13s. The run metadata confirms the head, completed status and success. Hosted replay executes both registered warning-strict normal and optimized commands. No check failed.

All registered checks, committed-byte/source-history preflight and read-only Git-free export replays also pass locally. These automated checks certify the bounded replay; independent human and formal proof-kernel review remain unclaimed.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Blast radius: research. One isolated opt-in package; shared code, frozen predecessors and the selected frontier are unchanged.
